revised_temporal_spread.reason: P013-A proved at least 32 unique identities at cell level, while the first P013-C materialization proved that strict near-equal allocation across every 61-session window is stronger than the observed window-level capacity in the earliest STAR era. The revision preserves the cell quota and identity-independence target while removing an unneeded per-window equality constraint.
selection_steps: within the current cell, consider only exposure-aware available metadata tokens whose economic identity is not already used by an earlier scarcity-priority cell
at each slot choose a non-exhausted window with the smallest assigned count
break equal assigned-count ties by the smallest remaining unique-identity capacity, then frozen window-seed hash, then chronological window start and window id
within the chosen window choose an identity with the fewest alternative eligible windows in the same cell, then deterministic frozen-seed hash, then economic identity
remove the chosen economic identity from every window in the current batch
continue until 32 unique identities are reserved for the cell
revised_temporal_spread.representation_floor: every non-empty eligible metadata window receives one assignment before any still-nonempty window receives a second assignment whenever unique-identity coupling permits
revised_temporal_spread.exhausted_window_policy: a metadata window with no remaining globally unused eligible identity is removed from subsequent waterfill rounds; remaining slots stay inside the same era-board cell
revised_temporal_spread.cell_shortfall_policy: if the union of globally unused eligible economic identities across the cell cannot reach 32, fail before market read; no cross-cell fill

claim_ceiling: R1 repairs metadata-plan feasibility only. It does not change the eight equal era-board cell quotas, create market-prevalence weights, relax global identity uniqueness, authorize result-bearing reads, or qualify any atomic proposition/candidate/Stage projection.
